answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a work-bonded reputation market: every identity must stake resources and complete verifiable tasks before earning rewards, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand stakes. Reputation grows like a pearl, layer by layer, and cannot be faked overnight. Like climbers on a narrow ledge above a mesa, each account must hold its own footing through sustained, checkable output; accounts caught copying answers or voting in lockstep lose their stake. One fake identity is cheap, but an army that survives peer review costs more than it can steal.
